question.text: The maximum profit for a seller (writer) of a call option is:

answer.text: Equal to the strike price minus premium
Equal to the spot price at expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.68, an option writer's maximum profit is the premium received, and p.70 shows the short call's maximum reward is limited to the premium. This occurs when the option expires out of the money and is not exercised. The Trap: Unlimited profit is the call BUYER's payoff. Strike minus premium is the put buyer's maximum reward. Note: The writer's reward is capped at the premium while the loss can be very large (unlimited for a naked short call) as the underlying rises.
